plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question has two parts in a fixed order: first, how much of the per-gene expression variance the condition (treated/control), sex (F/M), and age (years) each explain; second, which genes differ between treated and control. The inputs are a 12,000 gene x 12 sample raw integer Salmon count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) and a 12-row metadata table (metadata.csv: sample, condition, sex, age) for human adipose tissue, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch.

T1S1 runs the standard count-data sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) coloured by condition and sex, because any outlier or dominant nuisance axis must be visible before either the variance decomposition or the test is interpreted.

T1S2 answers the first question directly with variancePartition: a per-gene linear mixed model on voom log-CPM with precision weights, condition and sex as random effects (categorical) and centered age as a fixed effect (continuous), reporting the distribution across genes of the variance fraction attributable to each term plus residual. With n=12 and three terms this is a descriptive design diagnostic, not an inferential result — the step must say so and must report how sex and age are distributed across the two conditions, since imbalance makes the shares hard to separate.

T1S3 answers the second question: DESeq2 on the raw counts with design ~ sex + age_centered + condition, control set as the explicit reference level so a positive log2FC means higher in treated. Covariates enter the design as fixed effects rather than being regressed out of the counts. Minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the condition coefficient, BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, p-value histogram inspected before adjustment, count-outlier NAs (Cook's flagging, which applies at 6 replicates per cell) reported separately from independent-filter NAs. Because 6 per group sits at the low end, T1S4 refits the same design with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test and reports the overlap as the high-confidence set.

T2S1 is interpretation, not part of the asked question: preranked fgsea on the DESeq2 Wald statistic over the full tested list against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways human as separate collections (the human WikiPathways GMT is present in the reference store; Hallmark was reported present by the procedure service). It is ranked rather than over-representation precisely so a short significant list does not kill it.

T1S5 assembles the report: variance-partition summary first (it is the first question asked), then the DE tables with unshrunken and shrunken log2FC and lfcSE, MA and dispersion plots, method overlap, enrichment with its collection releases and rank metric, and a full reproducibility record. The whole analysis is 12 samples — effect estimates are imprecise and the plan states this rather than papering over it.

steps.question: Which treated-vs-control genes are called by both DESeq2 and edgeR quasi-likelihood, and which by only one method?
steps.description: Refit the same comparison with edgeR on the same filtered count matrix and the same design ~ sex + age_centered + condition: TMM normalization factors, estimateDisp, glmQLFit, glmQLFTest on the condition coefficient, BH adjustment at 0.05. Compare against the DESeq2 result from T1S3: report the number of significant genes from each method, the size of the intersection, and the genes called by only one method with that method named. Produce a scatter plot of the DESeq2 log2FC against the edgeR log2FC over all tested genes, and a Venn or upset diagram of the two significant sets. Treat the intersection as the high-confidence set; do not present the union as the result.
steps.context: Six replicates per group is the regime where DESeq2 and edgeR agree on most genes but disagree at low counts, so a second method is a robustness check rather than a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL run on the identical filtered gene set and identical design as T1S3, with TMM normalization factors
Table reporting n significant for DESeq2, n significant for edgeR, and n in the intersection at padj < 0.05
Method-exclusive gene lists exported with the calling method named
log2FC concordance scatter plot across all tested genes saved, with the Pearson or Spearman correlation reported
The intersection is labelled the high-confidence set and the union is explicitly not presented as the result
constraints: Use exactly the same pre-filtered gene set and the same design terms as the DESeq2 step so the comparison is like-for-like
BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 in both methods
Do not merge the two result tables into one significance call
caveats: Disagreement concentrates at low counts and low fold changes; describe where in the mean-expression range the methods diverge
Agreement between two methods on the same 12 samples is not independent validation — it is a robustness check only

grounding.reason: At 6 replicates per group the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is the named second method, with the intersection reported as the high-confidence set (R-0001, R-0042).

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Which gene sets are coordinately shifted between treated and control adipose samples, based on the full ranked list of tested genes?
steps.description: Rank every gene tested in T1S3 by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column) — the chosen side of the disputed rank-metric question, because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike an unshrunken fold change or a tie-prone signed p-value. Run fgsea on the full ranked list (never a thresholded list) with a gene set size window of 15 to 500 genes after intersecting each set with the tested genes. Run the human MSigDB Hallmark collection first; then run the human Reactome pathway sets and the human WikiPathways collection from the reference store as separate second and third passes with the same window and the same universe — do not merge collections into one test list. Map gene symbols to the identifier space each collection uses (org.Hs.eg.db where Entrez identifiers are needed) and report the share of tested genes that failed to map. Collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per overlap group with its leading-edge genes and their gene-level statistics, keeping the full table as a supplement. Report the release/version of each collection used. Set and record a random seed for the permutations.
steps.context: Interpretation layer on top of the treated-vs-control contrast; the user did not ask for pathways, so this is supporting context and must be framed as hypothesis-generating. Reference data needed: human hallmark gene sets, human Reactome pathway sets, and human WikiPathways sets. The human WikiPathways GMT is present in the reference store. If a collection is absent at run time, report that collection as unavailable, name it, and continue with the ones that are present rather than substituting a different organism's sets.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full ranked list of all tested genes from T1S3, ranked by the Wald statistic, with the metric named in the output
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes; universe is the tested genes
Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways run as separate passes, each with its collection release stated and its results kept separate
Share of tested genes that failed identifier mapping reported per collection
Significant sets (BH padj < 0.05) collapsed for redundancy, one representative per group reported with its leading-edge genes and their Wald statistics, full table kept as supplement
Random seed recorded; any collection absent from the reference store named as absent rather than silently substituted
Number of genes passing padj < 0.05 in T1S3 stated, so the reader knows whether an over-representation alternative was even viable
constraints: Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic; do not rank by unshrunken log2 fold change alone and do not use a signed p-value with ties
Never cut the ranked list at a significance or fold-change threshold before the test
Universe is the tested genes, not the whole genome or annotation
Do not merge Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways into a single set list
Use human collections only — the reference store also holds mouse and rat WikiPathways; selecting the wrong organism silently produces meaningless results
Do not run an over-representation test on a significant list of fewer than about 50 genes
caveats: Enrichment results depend strongly on the method and the collection; present each set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not a finding
Length and expression bias affect count-based enrichment; the tested-gene universe removes only part of it
With 12 samples the underlying gene-level statistics are noisy, which propagates into the enrichment

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list against Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways; the disputed rank metric (R-0108) is resolved here in favour of the DESeq2 Wald statistic, stated in the step.

steps.name: Integrated report
steps.question: Taken together, what share of adipose expression variance does each design factor explain, and which genes and pathways separate treated from control?
steps.description: Assemble the final report in the order the research question asks. First the variance decomposition from T1S2: median and IQR of the variance fraction for condition, sex, age, and residual, the violin plot, the design-collinearity check, and the explicit statement that these are descriptive with n=12. Then the differential expression: design formula, reference level and contrast direction, filter and thresholds, number of genes tested, number significant at padj < 0.05, the NA breakdown by cause, MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram. The gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value. Then the DESeq2/edgeR overlap with the intersection labelled the high-confidence set. Then the enrichment summary with each collection, its release, the rank metric, the universe, the size window, the representative sets and their leading-edge genes, and the caveat that enrichment results are method-dependent. Close with a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seeds, gene set collection versions, and the note that gene-level Salmon counts were supplied without transcript-length offsets.
steps.context: Single deliverable covering both halves of the question for the 12-sample human adipose dataset. Its job is to keep the descriptive variance decomposition and the inferential test clearly separated, and to state the power limits plainly rather than bury them.
acceptance_criteria: Report opens with the variance decomposition (the first question asked) before the differential expression results
Design formula, explicit reference level, contrast direction, thresholds, n tested, and n differentially expressed all stated before the gene tables
Gene table includes unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value
MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram included with a one-line reading of each
DESeq2/edgeR overlap reported with the intersection named as the high-confidence set
Enrichment section names each collection with its release, the rank metric, the universe, the size window, and lists leading-edge genes per representative set
Reproducibility record present: sessionInfo, package versions, seeds, collection versions
The n=12 power limitation and any sex/age imbalance across condition are stated explicitly in the limitations
constraints: Do not rank or headline genes by the unshrunken log2 fold change
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Do not describe the variance fractions as tested or significant — they carry no p-values
Do not describe enrichment hits as established mechanisms
State every threshold and every version; do not omit the reproducibility record
caveats: Any pathway or gene highlighted here comes from 12 samples in one batch and requires independent replication before it is treated as established
If sex or age is imbalanced across condition, the adjusted condition effect and the variance shares are partly entangled — say so rather than reporting point estimates alone

grounding.reason: Report content follows the procedure's report rules: method/versions/design/thresholds, shrunken and unshrunken effects, MA and dispersion diagnostics, method overlap, leading-edge genes, and a reproducibility record.
